chunks: 2563 - And in the narration of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, he said:

"If you enter into ihram from Ghamrah or Barid al-Ba'th, you should pray and say what the muhrim says after your prayer. And if you wish, you may recite the talbiyah from your place, but what is more virtuous is that you walk a little and then recite the talbiyah."

key_terms.أَحْرَمْتَ: entered into the state of ihram
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: what is more virtuous or preferable
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: the person in the state of ihram
key_terms.بَرِيدِ الْبَعْثِ: Barid al-Ba'th, a designated location for entering ihram
key_terms.غَمْرَةَ: Ghamrah, a designated location for entering ihram

ai.seo_question: What should one do when entering ihram from Ghamrah or Barid al-Ba'th?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a ruling about the procedure of entering ihram from specific locations during hajj. It instructs performing prayer and reciting the words of the muhrim after the prayer, while noting that reciting the talbiyah immediately is permissible, though it is more virtuous to walk a little first and then recite it.
